options.content:
### How to read this dashboard
- **Primary filter** is **$job** (server). **$instance** is hidden by default (it's a random UUID that changes on every restart) - only touch it to isolate one restart.
- **TPS** (Ticks Per Second) ranges **0-20**. **20** is best. Below **15** is urgent.
- **MSPT** (Milliseconds Per Tick) is the inverse view of TPS: **50ms** is the tick budget for **20 TPS**. Above **50ms** p95 means the server cannot sustain 20 TPS.
- Start at the **Critical (KPI)** row for fleet-wide and per-server headline numbers, then use **Top offenders** to find the worst server fast. **Proxies** and **Server inventory** cover Velocity proxies and which workloads emit what.
- Use the heatmap in **Abstract view**, then drill down by **$world** and **$entity_type** in **Detail view** below it.
- Only servers running the Minecraft OTel agent's game metrics (currently Survival-1, ElytraRace-1) show TPS/MSPT/chunks/entities - see **Server inventory** for who emits what. Velocity proxies don't emit these, so their panels stay empty; they're covered by the **Proxies** row instead.
- All rows except **Critical (KPI)** are collapsed by default to keep this dashboard scannable - expand the one you need.

panels.description: Total players across backend servers. Excludes proxy jobs (identified by also emitting minecraft_proxy_players_online_ratio): proxies also emit minecraft_players_online_ratio (their own player count), which would double count on top of each backend's count.
panels.title: Total players online (fleet)

panels.description: Server TPS (0–20). 20 TPS is ideal. Below 15 TPS requires urgent action.
panels.title: TPS (1m)

panels.description: MSPT (milliseconds per tick). Tick budget is 50ms (20 TPS). Above 50ms means the server cannot sustain 20 TPS.
panels.title: MSPT p95

panels.description: Online players (sum). Gives context for load and performance.
panels.title: Players Online

panels.description: 95th percentile tick duration derived from the histogram. Useful to spot spikes and validate MSPT.
panels.title: Tick p95 (Histogram)

panels.description: Server TPS (0–20). 20 TPS is ideal. Below 15 TPS requires urgent action.
panels.title: TPS (1m) per server

panels.description: MSPT p95 (milliseconds per tick). Tick budget is 50ms (20 TPS). Above 50ms means the server cannot sustain 20 TPS.
panels.title: MSPT p95 per server

panels.description: Average MSPT. Useful for baseline load. Combine with p95 to spot spikes.
panels.title: MSPT avg per server

panels.description: Total loaded entities per server. High entity counts often correlate with higher MSPT.
panels.title: Entities loaded (total) per server

panels.description: Online players per server. Context for load and performance.
panels.title: Players online per server

panels.description: Shows the worst servers by MSPT p95. Start here when you need a culprit fast.
panels.title: Top $topk MSPT p95 (highest)

panels.description: Shows the lowest TPS servers (actual TPS). Below 15 TPS is urgent.
panels.title: Bottom $topk TPS (lowest)
Top offenders (who is hurting right now)

panels.description: Players online per proxy (minecraft_proxy_players_online_ratio). Separate metric from backend player counts.
panels.title: Proxy players online

panels.description: Backend servers registered per proxy (minecraft_proxy_servers_registered_ratio), by server name.
panels.title: Proxy servers registered

panels.description: Every Minecraft workload (namespace-less JVM, i.e. not a k8s-deployed microservice, excluding reposilite) and whether it currently emits TPS/game metrics or is a Velocity proxy. Not filtered by $job - always shows the full fleet so missing metrics are visible.
panels.title: Server inventory

panels.description: Server TPS (0–20). 20 TPS is ideal. Below 15 TPS requires urgent action.
panels.title: TPS trend (1m/5m/15m)

panels.description: MSPT (milliseconds per tick). Tick budget is 50ms (20 TPS). Above 50ms means the server cannot sustain 20 TPS.
panels.title: MSPT avg / p95

panels.description: Heatmap of tick duration buckets. Dense areas at higher ms indicate dangerous spikes that cause lag.
panels.title: Tick duration heatmap (ms, rate over 5m)

panels.description: Total loaded chunks. Increases with players, farms, and active world area.
panels.title: Chunks loaded (total)

panels.description: Total loaded entities. High entity counts often correlate with higher MSPT.
panels.title: Entities loaded (total)

panels.description: Loaded chunks per world. Use $world to isolate worlds.
panels.title: Chunks loaded by world

panels.description: Rates over time. High 'generated' often means exploration or missing world pre-generation.
panels.title: Chunk load/unload/generate rate

panels.description: Entity load trend per world.
panels.title: Entities loaded by world

panels.description: Entity counts by type. Use $entity_type to isolate offenders (items, villagers, etc.).

targets.expr: topk(15, max by (job, entity_type) (minecraft_entities_loaded_by_type_ratio{job=~"((minecraft|proxy)/)?$job", instance=~"$instance", entity_type=~"$entity_type"}))

panels.title: Entities loaded by type

panels.description: Entity churn. High adds without matching removes can indicate spikes, leaks, or farms.
panels.title: Entities add/remove rate
